SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected icing can degrade both aerodynamic performance and air-data integrity, but the class turns on the icing exposure and on whether loss of protection/air-data in icing is Hazardous or Catastrophic for this airframe — the SDD provides the architecture but not the icing-envelope effects or air-data consequence needed to derive severity. Severity left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Two ice detectors are installed on opposite sides of the forward fuselage; loss of one leaves the second detector providing icing detection with reduced redundancy. Detection capability is retained.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one icing-detection channel
fha.effCrew: Reduced detection redundancy; manual selection of ice protection remains available; slight increase in monitoring.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Two detectors on opposite sides; loss of one leaves the second providing detection with the manual-selection path retained — a slight reduction in safety margin/redundancy with the function still available. The two detectors are 'identical in type', a common-cause item for CMA but not driving this single-channel-loss class. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Loss of all probe/static/windshield heating and both ice detectors: in icing, unheated probes and static ports can ice over, corrupting airspeed and angle-of-attack sensing, and no icing advisory or automatic activation is available. Air-data corruption to the three ADIRUs affects primary flight information common across the aircraft.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of probe heating and icing detection
fha.effCrew: No icing detection or advisory; unheated probes may produce misleading airspeed/AoA; crew workload rises and primary air-data integrity is threatened in icing.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This condition threatens air-data integrity feeding the primary displays as well as removing icing detection, which can be Hazardous or Catastrophic depending on remaining air-data means and icing exposure — the SDD notes the standby instrument shares nothing with the primaries, but does not state the air-data source topology under total probe-heat loss or the icing exposure, so the class cannot be derived. Severity left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Primary display presentation lost; independent integrated standby attitude, airspeed and altitude on the DC essential bus remains available, sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of primary flight and navigation display leaving standby information only
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload flying on reduced standby information; diversion likely.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD establishes that a standby instrument remains after loss of the primary displays, so the effect is a reduction in capability and increase in workload rather than total loss — but the residual capability of standby-only flight in IFR at low flight levels (whether it is a significant or large reduction in safety margin) is not determinable from the function definition alone. Severity left empty pending the standby-only handling/workload assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: An overpressured oxygen cylinder is discharged overboard through the thermal discharge indicator; the second cylinder with crossover remains, either being capable of supplying the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve.
fha.effPax: No passenger oxygen fitted; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.fcDesc: Cylinder overpressure vented overboard
fha.effCrew: Reduced oxygen reserve; loss annunciated by low-pressure alerting and the skin discharge indicator; dispatch/diversion consequences.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD shows a two-cylinder crossover architecture where either cylinder can supply the crew at reduced reserve, so a single overboard vent is a reduction in reserve rather than a loss of supply. Whether the residual reserve after one cylinder is lost still meets the required diversion duration — hence whether this is Minor or Major — cannot be determined from the function definition; severity left empty pending the oxygen sizing/reserve assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Aircraft flown to an erroneous state — deviation from intended trajectory, terrain/obstacle clearance or airspeed margin — because the crew act on misleading data. Independent standby instrument shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries, but detection of the discrepancy is not assured.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; effect is on the airframe and crew.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous or misleading flight and navigation information presented to the crew
fha.effCrew: Crew act on false information; cross-check against the standby instrument required to detect and recover; potential to command an unsafe state before the discrepancy is identified.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Misleading flight/nav information acted upon can drive loss of control or CFIT; worst-case across phases is loss of the aircraft. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: An actual nacelle, APU or bleed-duct fire/overheat is not annunciated; crew do not initiate extinguishing, allowing an undetected fire to progress in a fire zone containing flammable fluid and high energy.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; effect is on the airframe and crew.
fha.fcDesc: Masked fire and overheat detection — failure to annunciate an actual fire or overheat condition
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the fire; no fire-handle action taken; first indication is by secondary effects (thrust loss, smoke, structural damage) by which point response margin is degraded.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A masked (undetected) engine/APU fire defeats the sole means of crew-initiated extinguishing; unchecked fire in a nacelle can lead to loss of the aircraft. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: With no oxygen at the masks during a loss-of-pressurisation, smoke or fume event, both pilots are exposed to hypoxia or the contaminant with no protective means; aircraft control is lost if the crew are incapacitated.
fha.effPax: No passenger oxygen fitted — hold is not occupied in flight; effect is on the crew.
fha.fcDesc: No breathing oxygen delivered to crew masks on demand
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to obtain breathing oxygen when donning masks; incapacitation during the descent/diversion the system is intended to protect; crew-only aircraft has no relief crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of crew oxygen coincident with the event it protects against incapacitates both pilots; worst case is loss of the aircraft. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: The nine functional-type systems' purpose statements each denote an aircraft-level function the airframe accomplishes; the four resources and crew oxygen do not.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a resource (e.g. OXY) is intended as an aircraft function, or a functional system splits differently, the function list gains/loses rows and their up-links to FHA change.
assumptions.usedFor: All nine add_function rows; exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS/OXY.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves
It does not tell you what the aircraft-level functions are.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly declines to enumerate aircraft-level functions (Appendix A), so functions had to be derived from §5 purpose statements and the §2.1 function/resource split.

assumptions.text: Where a system purpose names two behaviours, capturing the sizing-relevant one as a single sub-function is acceptable for this one-level pass.
assumptions.ifWrong: If both behaviours are independently failable, additional sub-functions are required and independence notes must be added before FHA.

citations.quote: absorbs landing and taxi loads ... spreads footprint pressure ... and provides braking and directional control

assumptions.rationale: The task requests one level of decomposition; several purpose statements (LDG, ECS, NZD, CRG) name more than one behaviour and full split would exceed one level per turn.

assumptions.text: The four resource-type systems (FUE, HYD, EPS, EWS) are correctly excluded from the aircraft FUNCTION list and captured instead in the Resources model.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any of these must be represented as an aircraft function, the function list is incomplete and additional add_function actions are needed.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS from all authored functions

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft

assumptions.rationale: §2.1 labels these four as resources that supply other systems rather than act on the aircraft; the modeling rule forbids authoring resources as functions, so no functions were derived from them.

assumptions.text: The nose door and hold hard points are structure, not functions, so only the door's motion/lock/interlock BEHAVIOURS are authored.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the structural load path is expected as a function it would need separate treatment, but per the modeling rule it belongs in structural analysis and PRA, not the function list.
assumptions.usedFor: NZD 'open/close' and 'lock/confirm' functions; CRG restraint functions

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.rationale: §5.7.3 and §5.8.3 state the door is a single load path treated as structure and the hard points have no redundancy; structural integrity is a PRA/structural item, not a functional-FHA item.

assumptions.text: Crew oxygen is retained as an aircraft-level function (behaviour: supply breathing oxygen) even though §2.1 tags OXY as a resource.
assumptions.ifWrong: If OXY is to be modeled purely as a consumed resource, the 'Supply crew oxygen on demand' function should be removed and captured in the Resources model instead.
assumptions.usedFor: Function 'Supply crew breathing oxygen' / sub 'Supply crew oxygen on demand'

citations.quote: OXY   Crew Oxygen   Resource   Supplies flight crew

assumptions.rationale: §2.1 lists OXY under 'Resource', but the modeling rule names electrical/hydraulic/pneumatic power and fuel as the resources; breathing-oxygen supply to crew is a behaviour the aircraft accomplishes, so it was authored as a function pending engineer disposition.

assumptions.text: SF-002 reverse thrust is a ground-only function, so its total/partial-loss conditions are intrinsically evident during the roll-out and the crew-unaware variant is inapplicable for those conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loss of reverse is not self-evident during roll-out, SF-002 needs a crew-Unaware total/partial-loss row carrying those conditions.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002 Aware row and the decision to keep only an asymmetric-reverse malfunction on the Unaware row

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement

assumptions.rationale: The function list and SDD confirm reverse is ground-only but do not state detection means; I inferred self-evidence from the deceleration cue during roll-out.

assumptions.text: The two inboard-only thrust reversers can produce an asymmetric-reverse condition on the ground.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reversers are interlocked to deploy only symmetrically, the asymmetric-reverse malfunction rows for SF-002 are removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002 malfunctions[] asymmetric-reverse entries and the SF-002 Unaware row

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only

assumptions.rationale: SDD states reversers are inboard-only; asymmetry is a plausible malfunction but the failure logic is not defined in the provided material.

assumptions.text: For the pitch/roll/yaw axes, a degraded or uncommanded condition can develop below crew detection thresholds, justifying a crew-Unaware row for those variants.
assumptions.ifWrong: If envelope-protection alerting always annunciates degraded laws before threshold, the SF-003/004/005 Unaware rows collapse into the Aware row.

citations.quote: Degraded laws are annunciated.

assumptions.rationale: No detection-threshold or alerting definition exists in the model yet; the Unaware split is inferred from the general possibility of slow divergence.

assumptions.text: Loss of yaw control authority combined with an outboard asymmetric-thrust case is a combined failure condition to be captured in the matrix Combined column.
assumptions.ifWrong: If directional control is sized with margin independent of asymmetric thrust, no combined SF-005/SF-001 condition is needed.
assumptions.usedFor: Combined-column flag for SF-005 with SF-001

citations.quote: The sizing case for directional control is an outboard engine failure at V1 with the maximum blade payload

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the outboard-engine-out-with-max-blade case as the directional-control sizing case, implying a combined yaw/thrust dependency not captured by single-function rows.

assumptions.text: High-lift drive through a common torque shaft can produce asymmetric deployment as a distinct malfunction from an erroneous symmetric schedule.
assumptions.ifWrong: The 'asymmetric high-lift deployment' malfunction entry on SF-006 would be dropped as non-credible.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006 malfunctions[] entry 'Asymmetric high-lift deployment between sides'

citations.quote: through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.rationale: The function list alone does not distinguish asymmetry; the SDD names asymmetry brakes, implying asymmetry is a credible failure mode requiring its own condition.

assumptions.text: Flotation degradation on the semi-prepared surface is a distinct partial-loss capability separate from generic partial loss of ground support.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-007 partial 'Reduced footprint flotation on semi-prepared surface' would merge into generic partial loss of ground support.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-007 partialLoss 'Reduced footprint flotation on semi-prepared surface'

citations.quote: spreads footprint pressure to the level the operating surfaces require

assumptions.rationale: The function pairs ground support with flotation; the mission relies on footprint pressure to the semi-prepared surface, so flotation loss is a mission-specific condition the function list does not itself separate.

assumptions.text: Reduced or asymmetric braking can develop below crew detection thresholds and warrants a crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-008 Unaware row is removed if all braking degradation is shown to be annunciated in time for crew response.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-008 Unaware row (undetected reduced/asymmetric braking, undetected anti-skid loss)

citations.quote: Anti-skid operates per wheel pair

assumptions.rationale: Detection means and effect timing are not fully specified; anti-skid loss and gradual degradation may not annunciate until the rollout, so the undetectable case is retained per the awareness-per-condition rule.

assumptions.text: The nose door is a ground-only function with no in-flight operation, so open/close failure conditions are ground-phase; the in-flight pressure-boundary and lock-status conditions are treated under SF-011 (lock and confirm closure), not here.
assumptions.ifWrong: If in-flight inadvertent movement is credible under SF-010 rather than SF-011, an additional SF-010 malfunction row for loss of pressure-boundary integrity would be required.
assumptions.usedFor: Scope of SF-010 rows (drive/close capability only)

citations.quote: is operated from a ground handling panel... and cannot be operated in flight

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the door cannot be operated in flight; SF-010 covers open/close and SF-011 covers lock/confirm, so this turn's SF-010 conditions are scoped to the drive/close capability.

assumptions.text: Crew indication and mitigation detail cannot be grounded per condition from the function list alone and are left empty pending FHA effects and detection means.
assumptions.ifWrong: Once effects and detection means exist, the empty indication/mitigation fields are filled and awareness splits may be refined.
assumptions.usedFor: Empty indication/mitigation fields across all SF-006..SF-010 rows
assumptions.rationale: The FCIM feeds the AFHA; specific annunciations and procedures require effects/detection that do not yet exist in the model, so those fields are abstained per the abstention rule.

assumptions.text: A defeated or failed lock-sensing path can present an erroneous lock-secure confirmation without any alert, making the crew-unaware variant of SF-011 applicable.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-011 Unaware row is removed and the erroneous-confirmation condition becomes crew-Aware only.

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states lock status is displayed but does not describe a monitor that cross-checks the two sensing paths for disagreement, so undetected erroneous confirmation cannot be excluded.

assumptions.text: A single instrumented tension loop can lose coverage at one or more stations without self-announcing, so undetected loss of SF-013 monitoring coverage is credible.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-013 Unaware row is removed; loss of coverage becomes annunciated and crew-Aware.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-013 Unaware row (loss of monitoring coverage; failure to annunciate)

citations.quote: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item

assumptions.rationale: The SDD calls the loop a single instrumented loop whose coverage is a recorded item, but does not state a loop-integrity/self-test that would make coverage loss self-evident.

assumptions.text: A slow pressurisation differential drift can develop below the crew alerting threshold, supporting an SF-014 crew-unaware malfunction condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-014 Unaware row is removed if all differential excursions are shown to be annunciated within crew-detectable time.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-014 Unaware row (slow uncommanded differential drift)

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states differential and cabin altitude are provided to the crew and oxygen logic but gives no alerting threshold, so an undetected slow drift cannot be grounded or excluded.

assumptions.text: Loss of longitudinal restraint (SF-012) combined with loss of the restraint-tension monitor (SF-013) is a distinct combined failure condition worth capturing in the Combined column.
assumptions.ifWrong: The Combined-column entry is dropped if the engineer judges the monitor loss does not aggravate the restraint loss condition.
assumptions.usedFor: Combined condition flagged for SF-012 + SF-013

citations.quote: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight

assumptions.rationale: The two functions are related sub-functions per ARP4761A Table A3; the monitor is the means by which restraint loss is revealed, so their simultaneous loss changes crew awareness.

assumptions.text: Loss or degradation of ice protection can progress below crew detection thresholds, justifying a crew-Unaware variant for SF-016.
assumptions.ifWrong: If every protection shortfall is reliably annunciated, the SF-016 crew-Unaware conditions collapse into the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016 malfunctions[] 'ice protection failing off with no removal of accretion' and partials[]

citations.quote: Electrical zones are independently supplied and a lost zone is annunciated.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states a lost electrical zone is annunciated but does not establish that all protection degradation or the developing-accretion case is annunciated in time.

assumptions.text: Icing detection is advisory and can fail to detect present icing without the crew being alerted, justifying a crew-Unaware masked-detection condition for SF-017.
assumptions.ifWrong: If undetected icing is otherwise annunciated, the SF-017 masked-detection condition moves to the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017 malfunctions[] 'failure to detect icing conditions that are present'

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available

assumptions.rationale: The SDD says detection is advisory and the two detectors are of the same type; it does not establish an alert for undetected icing.

assumptions.text: Misleading flight/navigation information can be presented without the crew recognising it as erroneous, justifying the SF-018 crew-Unaware malfunction row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If misleading data is always cross-monitored and flagged, the SF-018 misleading conditions become crew-Aware.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018 malfunctions[] 'misleading flight-parameter presentation' / 'misleading navigation presentation'

citations.quote: an independent standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes an independent standby instrument but does not establish comparator monitoring that flags all misleading primary presentations to the crew.

assumptions.text: A missing/failure-to-annunciate alert in SF-019 is by nature crew-Unaware, since the absent alert is the undetectable condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If alerting-system health is itself monitored and annunciated, the failure-to-annunciate condition moves toward Aware.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019 malfunctions[] 'failure to annunciate an actual system failure'

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: The alerting function's own failure to annunciate cannot self-indicate; the SDD does not describe monitoring of the alerting system's coverage completeness.

assumptions.text: Fire/overheat detection can fail masked (fail to warn on a real event) below crew awareness, justifying the SF-020 crew-Unaware condition, while degraded logic remains detectable.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loss of detection sensitivity is annunciated, the masked-detection condition moves to the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020 malfunctions[] 'failure to detect an actual fire or overheat condition'

citations.quote: an AND logic between them for warning, degrading to single-loop logic on loss of one loop

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes AND-then-single-loop logic but does not establish annunciation that detection has become insensitive to an actual fire.

assumptions.text: SF-018 misleading presentation combined with SF-019 alerting loss is a candidate Combined failure condition for the matrix Combined column.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the combination is not credible or is covered elsewhere, the Combined-column entry is dropped.
assumptions.usedFor: Combined-column candidate spanning SF-018 and SF-019

citations.quote: hosts the alerting that tells the crew what has failed and what to do about it

assumptions.rationale: ARP4761A Table A3 flags combined conditions across related sub-functions; misleading data with no alerting removes the crew's means to detect it.

assumptions.text: SF-021 and SF-022 are on-demand (discrete) functions, so the 'stopped too soon / applied too long' UCA/malfunction type is not authored.
assumptions.ifWrong: If either is treated as a continuous function, a fourth failure-condition type would be added to the affected malfunctions[] array.

citations.quote: Masks are donned on crew action. There is no automatic deployment. The system is passive in normal flight

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes extinguishing as a discrete crew/auto discharge and oxygen as donned on demand, neither being a continuous regulated output.

assumptions.text: The automatic APU discharge occurs only on the ground with the aircraft unattended, giving a crew-Unaware inadvertent-discharge variant for SF-021.
assumptions.ifWrong: If APU auto-discharge can occur in flight or attended, the Unaware SF-021 row collapses into the Aware row.

citations.quote: The APU has a single dedicated bottle discharged automatically on detection with the aircraft unattended.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states automatic APU discharge is ground-unattended; no crew is present to detect an inadvertent event.

assumptions.text: Loss of stored crew-oxygen quantity can develop below crew detection when the DC-powered pressure indication is itself lost, supporting a crew-Unaware SF-022 partial.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a low-pressure alert survives loss of primary indication independently, the Unaware SF-022 row is not required.

citations.quote: DC power for indication only

assumptions.rationale: Indication depends on DC power; a leak plus loss of indication would be undetected until the mask is needed.

assumptions.text: Crew indication and mitigation/procedure detail left empty where the SDD gives no specific annunciation text or checklist step for the identified conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: Empty indication/mitigation fields would be filled once effects and detection means are established; no failure condition changes.
assumptions.usedFor: Indication/mitigation fields on all four rows
assumptions.rationale: The SDD documents architecture and some detection means but not the alerting text or crew procedures per failure condition.

assumptions.text: SF-001-TL denotes simultaneous total loss of thrust from all four independent propulsors, i.e. an aircraft-level state with no thrust available by any means.
assumptions.ifWrong: If TL means loss of a subset that still leaves usable thrust, the effect is no longer loss of the airplane and the proposed Catastrophic/CAT-1 class drops.

citations.quote: Four podded turbofans on pylons beneath the high wing provide thrust for all phases of flight

assumptions.rationale: The AFHA condition is stated at aircraft-function level; the SDD gives four engines each with independent feeds, so a genuine total loss requires a common cause the function text does not name.

assumptions.text: The thrust asymmetry in SF-001-M can reach the outboard-engine 28 m moment-arm magnitude that the SDD names as the directional-control sizing case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If credible asymmetry is limited to inboard engines or a smaller moment, the margin reduction is smaller and the class could drop from Hazardous to Major.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.rationale: The function text does not bound the asymmetry magnitude; the SDD's sizing statement is the only anchor for how large a credible asymmetry is.

assumptions.text: SF-002 (reverse thrust) applies only to the two inboard engines and, in flight, deployment is prevented by the WOW + radio-altimeter interlock and mechanical sleeve lock.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the interlock can be defeated, an in-flight uncommanded deployment case becomes credible and would likely drive a higher severity than the ground case.

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock

assumptions.rationale: The SDD fits reversers to inboard engines only and describes an in-flight inhibit; this determines which phase the SF-002-M condition is credible in.

assumptions.text: All SF-002 reverse-thrust failure conditions are ground-phase only (landing rollout and rejected take-off), not in-flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse thrust could deploy in flight, an in-flight asymmetric/uncommanded deployment case would be a far more severe condition and the phase and severity of SF-002-M2/M3 change.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-M2, SF-002-M3, SF-002-PL, SF-002-TL phases and effects

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.

assumptions.rationale: The FCIM conditions are titled 'ground reverse thrust' but the phase list is not given per condition; I inferred phase from the SDD's in-flight deployment inhibit.

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is a supplement to wheel braking, which is the primary decelerator, so loss/reduction of reverse is a stopping-margin issue rather than an immediate stopping failure.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse thrust carries a material credit in the certified landing distance, SF-002-PL and SF-002-TL could be classified (potentially MAJ-1 or higher) rather than left blank.

citations.quote: The margin between those two numbers is the operating margin on which the braking and flotation design rests.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD frames the landing-distance margin around braking and flotation, not reverse; the reverse-thrust credit in the certified landing distance is not stated.

assumptions.text: Asymmetric reverse thrust affects directional control only across the two inboard reverser-equipped engines (outboards have no reversers).
assumptions.ifWrong: If the asymmetry magnitude is larger than assumed (or interacts with the outboard thrust setting), the directional excursion severity for SF-002-M2/M3 would increase.

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only.

assumptions.rationale: Reversers are fitted to inboard engines only; the asymmetric-thrust moment arm and magnitude available for a reverse asymmetry are therefore bounded by the inboard pair, but the SDD does not quantify it.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so all occupant effects reduce to crew effects.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in the hold, passenger-effect columns and potentially severities would change.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: Needed to state the Effect-on-Occupants column for every row.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so no passenger/occupant injury effects arise for roll-control failure conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants are carried in flight, the occupant-effect column and potentially the severity for M2/PL2/M3/PL3 would need to account for injury/distress to those occupants.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-003-M2, SF-003-M3, SF-003-PL, SF-003-PL2, SF-003-PL3

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: The FHA effect-on-occupants field needs an occupancy basis; the roll function definition alone does not state who is aboard.

assumptions.text: Roll control is a primary trajectory-control function whose loss or malfunction bears on the aircraft's ability to maintain controlled flight in all phases.
assumptions.ifWrong: If roll authority were non-critical (e.g. fully covered by other axes), the Hazardous proposals for M2/PL2/M3/PL3 would drop toward Major.
assumptions.usedFor: severity on SF-003-M2, SF-003-PL2, SF-003-M3, SF-003-PL3

citations.quote: provides the control authority required across the flight envelope including the engine-out and blade-loaded cases

assumptions.rationale: The provided function list names 'Control roll' under 'Control aircraft trajectory' but does not itself state the safety consequence; the aircraft-effect and severity rest on treating roll as flight-critical.

assumptions.text: For the unaware below-threshold conditions (M3, PL3) the crew take no corrective action until the condition becomes apparent, per the FHA unaware-case rule.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection or an automatic protection intervenes earlier than assumed, M3/PL3 severity could be lower than Hazardous; if the divergence reaches loss of control, it could be Catastrophic.
assumptions.rationale: ARP4761A requires the unaware case to assume no crew action; the provided material gives no detection threshold or divergence/degradation rate to bound the outcome.

assumptions.text: Loss or malfunction of a single primary trajectory-control axis (roll or pitch) at the aircraft level is not recoverable to safe controlled flight in the worst applicable phase.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a reversion path preserves adequate roll/pitch control after these conditions, SF-003-TL, SF-004-M and SF-004-M2 could reduce from Catastrophic to Hazardous.

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes FCS redundancy and a mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim and lower rudder, but the provided functions state only the objective 'Control pitch'/'Control roll'; residual controllability after a full-axis loss/malfunction is not quantified in the function definitions.

assumptions.text: For SF-004-M3 the crew take no corrective action for the full duration the divergence remains below the detection threshold.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the divergence saturates or becomes benign before reaching an uncontrollable state, SF-004-M3 could reduce to Hazardous or Major.

citations.quote: Degraded laws are annunciated.

assumptions.rationale: ARP4761A requires the crew-unaware case to assume no action; the divergence rate and the time before it becomes detectable/effective are not provided, so the exposure that drives the worst-case effect is unbounded in the inputs.

assumptions.text: For SF-004-PL the residual pitch authority, while reduced, keeps the aircraft controllable throughout the flight envelope in all phases.
assumptions.ifWrong: If remaining authority is large but insufficient at critical low-energy phases, SF-004-PL could rise from Major to Hazardous.

citations.quote: the control authority required across the flight envelope

assumptions.rationale: The condition text states 'within manoeuvre limits' but does not quantify how much authority remains, which distinguishes a significant (Major) from a large (Hazardous) reduction in margins.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so passenger effects are limited to flight crew for every row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in the hold, the effect-on-passengers assessment would need to be added and could affect severity.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: The FHA requires an effect-on-occupants column; the SDD states the hold carries payload only, not occupants.

assumptions.text: The Aeolus HL-1 hold is unoccupied in flight, so passenger effects reduce to flight-crew-only exposure for these conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried, the occupant-effect field and possibly the severity of each condition would need re-derivation.

assumptions.text: The three dissimilar FCCs vote/monitor such that a single erroneous computation is contained unless the voting defence is also defeated.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the voting does not contain a single-channel erroneous command, the AND collapses toward an order-1 cut set, which is unacceptable for a Catastrophic top event and would require re-architecting the branch.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-M: 'Erroneous roll command generated by flight control computers reaches surfaces' AND-gate

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes three dissimilar computers voting but does not detail the vote/monitor coverage, forcing the AND (erroneous output AND containment failure).

assumptions.text: Roll surfaces comprise ailerons (on HYD B and C) and multi-function spoilers, each with its own actuator control electronics.
assumptions.ifWrong: If spoilers do not contribute to commanded roll or ACE topology differs, the roll-surface OR branch changes membership.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-M: 'Erroneous actuator-control-electronics command to a roll surface' OR-gate

citations.quote: Roll is by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names ailerons and spoilers for roll and dual actuation per surface but does not enumerate the actuator-control-electronics per surface, so the ACE contributors are modelled at the surface level the document resolves.

assumptions.text: An erroneous roll command reaching the aileron actuators requires both a faulted FCC and a failure of the command-voting/comparator to reject it.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the voting monitor makes an erroneous command require coincident failures, the FCC command branch of SF-003-M2 and the low-rate command source of SF-003-M3 become AND gates rather than single OR inputs, removing an order-1 cut set.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-M2 command branch ('Erroneous roll command generated by flight control computers'); SF-003-M3 slow-source 'Low-rate erroneous roll command from flight control computer'

citations.quote: Primary control is fly-by-wire with three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states three dissimilar FCCs vote on command but does not document the comparator/monitor logic or its coverage, so I could not decide whether the command branch is an OR (single) or an AND (coincident) contributor.

assumptions.text: There is no dedicated roll-rate/attitude divergence monitor beyond the primary display presentation and the consolidated crew alerting.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a dedicated roll-divergence monitor exists, the SF-003-M3 detection branch gains that contributor and its coverage may change whether the top event remains a plausible two-order AND.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-M3 detection branch 'Roll divergence not detected / annunciated to crew'

citations.quote: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes display presentation and a consolidated alert list but does not name a specific slow-roll-divergence monitor or its threshold, so the detection branch of SF-003-M3 was built from the AVI paths only.

assumptions.text: The mechanical reversion path does not drive roll surfaces and therefore contributes no independent uncommanded-roll source.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any mechanical path can move a roll surface, an additional basic-event source would need adding under both uncommanded-roll trees.
assumptions.usedFor: Both SF-003-M2 and SF-003-M3 source branches

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.rationale: The SDD limits mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim and the lower rudder segment; nothing indicates a roll reversion path, so no reversion contributor was placed in either roll tree.

assumptions.text: The A/B shared wing-root run is not a common-cause contributor to the ailerons, which are supplied by HYD B and HYD C.
assumptions.ifWrong: If HYD B distribution to the ailerons shares the A/B wing-root run and can be lost with system A events, an aileron-supply CCF basic event must be added under SF-003-TL, weakening the AND independence.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-TL tree, aileron HYD B/C branches

citations.quote: the ailerons from B and C

assumptions.rationale: The SDD records the A/B wing-root commonality but the ailerons draw on B and C, not A and B together; no aileron-specific CCF is stated.

assumptions.text: Multi-function spoilers provide sufficient standalone roll authority such that complete loss requires losing both ailerons AND spoilers.
assumptions.ifWrong: If spoilers cannot sustain roll control alone, the top AND collapses toward an OR and the aileron branch alone may be an order-1 cut set for a Catastrophic condition.

citations.quote: Roll is by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists ailerons and spoilers as roll effectors but does not state the residual roll authority of spoilers alone.

assumptions.text: An erroneous (wrong-sense/magnitude) pitch output implies the 3-computer dissimilar vote is defeated by a common input or common-mode, rather than a single computer disagreeing.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single computer can drive an erroneous surface command without being outvoted, the FBW erroneous-command branch simplifies to single-computer basic events.

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes 3 dissimilar computers voting on command; a single erroneous computer would normally be outvoted, so an erroneous system output needs a common-mode or shared-input path.

assumptions.text: Elevators are supplied from HYD A and HYD C and the stabiliser is the third pitch effector, so erroneous surface response has three distinct paths.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the stabiliser or an elevator draws on a different supply, the HYD-path labelling under the erroneous-surface branch must be corrected.

citations.quote: the elevators from A and C

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states elevators from A and C and pitch by an all-moving stabiliser with elevators.

assumptions.text: An erroneous pitch command reaching the surface requires all three dissimilar flight control computers to output the erroneous command (modelled AND).
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single erroneous FCC output can drive the surface, the AND becomes an OR and the branch becomes an order-1 cut set, unacceptable for a Catastrophic condition.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M2 gate 'Erroneous pitch command survives the three-computer vote'; SF-004-M3 gate 'Slow erroneous pitch command survives three-computer vote'

citations.quote: Primary control is fly-by-wire with three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states three computers vote on command but does not define the voting threshold or fault-containment for a corrupted command, forcing a conservative AND representation of the vote.

assumptions.text: The slow uncommanded pitch divergence is annunciated only through the AVI alerting system (two channels) and the pitch-attitude display, with no dedicated pitch-monitor documented.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a dedicated pitch-rate/divergence monitor exists, the detection-failure branch gains an additional independent input and the AND depth changes.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M3 gate 'Failure to annunciate / display the pitch divergence to crew'

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: The SDD documents crew alerting and displays but does not describe any dedicated slow-divergence pitch monitor, so the detection branch is built solely from the alerting and display paths that exist.

assumptions.text: Uncommanded stabiliser-trim runaway and elevator actuator hardover are within the scope of the aircraft-level pitch-function tree rather than a lower system tree.
assumptions.ifWrong: If these belong to an FCS SFHA tree, they are removed from the AFHA tree and replaced by a transfer to the system tree.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M2 basic events 'Uncommanded stabiliser-trim runaway' and 'Elevator actuator hardover / uncommanded deflection'; SF-004-M3 slow-onset OR branch

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.rationale: The provided FHA is aircraft-level and no SFHA/system rows exist yet; the SDD names these as pitch-surface contributors so they are carried at this level pending the system decomposition.

assumptions.text: The three FCC command paths to the elevator actuators are independent such that their loss must be combined under an AND gate.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a shared resource defeats the three paths, the AND collapses toward an order-1 cut set and SF-004-TL structure fails the Catastrophic no-single-point rule.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-TL gate 'Loss of FCS command path to elevator actuators'

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states three dissimilar computers on different electrical sources but does not enumerate the elevator command-path failure logic at basic-event level.

assumptions.text: Elevator power is via HYD A and HYD C only, so loss of powered elevator control requires loss of both A and C.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a third supply or cross-connection exists the powered-elevator branch structure changes.

citations.quote: the elevators from A and C

assumptions.rationale: The SDD assigns elevators to A and C but the tree needs this to set the AND logic.

assumptions.text: The stabiliser-trim mechanical reversion is a genuinely separate pitch means from powered elevators, so total pitch loss requires losing both.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reversion shares a resource with the elevators the top AND weakens toward a single point.

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim

assumptions.rationale: SDD names a mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim; the detailed independence from HYD/EPS is not fully described.

assumptions.text: A slow yaw divergence 'below detection threshold' requires both an uncommanded deflection source and independent failure/absence of the detection & alerting means.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a dedicated yaw-rate monitor exists and always annunciates, the 'crew unaware' branch and thus the whole FC structure changes.

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes

assumptions.rationale: The FC is defined by non-detection; the SDD does not specify the yaw-asymmetry monitor, so the detection branch is modelled from the alerting/display architecture generically.

assumptions.text: Complete loss of yaw authority requires loss of the upper segment path AND the lower segment path AND the mechanical reversion to the lower segment.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the segments are not fully independent (e.g. shared electronics), the top AND would collapse toward an OR and a single-point failure could appear, violating the Catastrophic no-order-1 rule.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-TL top AND gate and its two segment OR branches plus the reversion basic event

citations.quote: yaw by a split rudder in upper and lower segments, each with its own actuation and its own hydraulic supply
A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states each segment has its own actuation and hydraulic supply and that a mechanical reversion path exists to the lower rudder segment only, but does not give piece-part failure modes.

assumptions.text: Rudder upper is supplied by HYD A and rudder lower by HYD B.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the segment/supply mapping differs, the OR-branch basic-event labels for hydraulic loss are misassigned, though the AND logic and cut-set order are unchanged.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-TL segment OR branches; SF-005-PL3 degraded-supply basic event

citations.quote: A → rudder upper, elevators; B → rudder lower, ailerons; C → elevators, ailerons

assumptions.rationale: The interface matrix maps A→rudder upper and B→rudder lower, but the segment-to-actuation mapping detail below that is not enumerated.

assumptions.text: No yaw-specific slow-divergence / below-threshold monitor is defined in the architecture, so the detection branch of SF-005-PL3 is left undeveloped.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a yaw-degradation monitor exists, the detection OR branch must be populated with its real failure modes, which changes whether the 'unaware' AND is credibly independent.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-PL3 'Failure to detect / annunciate' OR branch (blank diamonds)

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes

assumptions.rationale: The SDD documents general crew alerting and FCS jam/asymmetry discretes but no yaw slow-divergence detection threshold; abstention rule requires leaving that content blank rather than inventing it.

assumptions.text: Complete loss of ground support / flotation (SF-007-TL) is a structural-integrity condition substantiated by structural analysis and Particular Risk Analysis, not a functional-contributor fault tree.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a functional-loss mechanism (e.g. common uplock/downlock or free-fall extension fault causing all-gear collapse) exists, the SF-007-TL tree gains functional OR contributors and is no longer a bare structural AND.

citations.quote: Saddles are pinned to hard points

assumptions.rationale: §5.6.2 describes the gear as pinned structure with no leg-level functional redundancy, and the SDD gives no functional contributor chain for a total loss of ground support; Appendix A flags leg/bogie count as preliminary.

assumptions.text: The nose gear unit and the left/right main bogie groups fail independently, so no single structural event takes all support simultaneously.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a common structural or zonal event (e.g. fuselage-side fairing structural failure) can take multiple units, the AND collapses toward a single-point structural failure and the qualitative acceptability fails.

citations.quote: six three-wheel main bogies, three per side, retracting into fuselage-side fairings

assumptions.rationale: §5.6.2 lists them as separate units retracting into fuselage-side fairings but does not state a shared structural failure path; independence is assumed to keep the Catastrophic top event free of an order-1 cut set.

assumptions.text: The three brake sources — normal (HYD B), alternate (HYD A) and accumulator emergency — are independent such that no single event defeats all three.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the shared gear-bay bundle routing constitutes a common cause across HYD A and B brake feeds, the two hydraulic legs are not independent and the AND no longer meets the Catastrophic objective — a CCF group and possibly restructuring are required.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-008-TL top AND gate; HYD A and HYD B pressure basic events

citations.quote: Brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through each main gear bay in adjacent bundles

assumptions.rationale: §5.6.3 states dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve, but §5.6.5 records that brake lines A and B share the main gear bay in adjacent bundles, a recorded zonal/CCF item.

assumptions.text: The electrically-signalled brake control path is represented as a per-source signalling basic event because the SDD does not resolve whether the signalling path is common across the normal and alternate sources.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single brake control electronics path is common to both HYD A and HYD B braking, that path is an order-1 cut set (single-point failure) for a Catastrophic condition and must be pulled out as a shared contributor above the AND.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-008-TL brake control signalling basic events

citations.quote: electrically signalled, hydraulically actuated brake control

assumptions.rationale: §5.6.2 states 'electrically signalled, hydraulically actuated brake control' without defining the electrical channel architecture or whether one brake control unit serves both hydraulic supplies.

assumptions.text: The SF-010-M2 top event requires both the door being not-fully-closed and that condition going undetected, so detection failure is modelled as a required AND co-contributor.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a not-fully-closed door alone (with correct indication) is the intended hazard, the top gate collapses to the drive/latch OR branch and the detection AND branch is removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010-M2 top AND gate and its 'Not-fully-closed condition not detected' branch

citations.quote: Lock status is displayed on the flight deck at all times and is included in the take-off configuration check.

assumptions.rationale: The failure-condition text itself states 'undetected or accepted at dispatch', which the SDD does not otherwise decompose; I inferred detection failure is part of the top event.

assumptions.text: A false locked/secure confirmation requires BOTH the proximity harness and the mechanical indicator to erroneously read locked, because the two sensing paths are dissimilar and independent.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single sensing path drives the displayed confirmation without agreement logic, the sensing branch becomes an OR and each path is an order-1 cut set — unacceptable for Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011-M sensing AND branch and the common-cause leaf

citations.quote: sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.rationale: §5.7.2/§5.7.5 describe two dissimilar independently routed sensing circuits but do not quantify their independence, so I modelled them as an AND with an explicit common-cause leaf.

assumptions.text: The twelve rotary latches share a common torque shaft, making their collective failure to engage a single contributor rather than twelve independent events.
assumptions.ifWrong: If latches were independently driven, the latch contribution would be a high-order AND rather than a single basic event, weakening its cut-set significance.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010-M2 'Twelve rotary latches fail to engage on closure (common torque shaft)' basic event

citations.quote: Twelve rotary latches engage on closure, driven by a common torque shaft.

assumptions.rationale: §5.7.2 states the latches are driven by a common torque shaft; the SDD does not resolve individual latch failure modes.

assumptions.text: Both dissimilar lock-sensing paths (proximity harness and mechanical indicator) must give a false 'locked' indication for erroneous confirmation to reach the crew, i.e. they are independent.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single sensing path alone can display 'locked/secure', SF-011-M3 has an order-1 cut set and the AND gate over the two sensing paths must become an OR — unacceptable for a Catastrophic condition without further mitigation.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011-M3 lower AND gate over the two lock-sensing paths

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits: a proximity sensing harness reading pin position directly, and a mechanical linkage driving a visual indicator

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states dual dissimilar independently routed sensing but does not state whether the take-off configuration monitor / display consolidates them such that either alone can drive a false secure indication.

assumptions.text: The pressure interlock is a single series element on the unlock command; the ECS residual-differential signal it consumes is a distinct contributor from the interlock logic itself.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the interlock is single-channel with no independent confirmation, SF-011-M2's inhibit branch is effectively order-1 and the AND with the residual-differential condition may not by itself meet the Catastrophic objective.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011-M2 interlock-failure OR gate and its ECS-signal contributor

citations.quote: A pressure interlock in series with the unlock command.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes one interlock in series and one ECS-supplied pressure state, but does not decompose the interlock into redundant channels, so no deeper independent structure can be grounded.

assumptions.text: These ground/dispatch-originated door-lock faults are carried into flight as latent conditions relevant to a per-flight-hour Catastrophic objective.
assumptions.ifWrong: If unlock permission cannot be erroneously granted in flight and no latent path exists, the flight-phase framing and exposure basis of SF-011-M2 change and the tree scope narrows to ground operations.
assumptions.usedFor: Top-event framing of SF-011-M2 and SF-011-M3

citations.quote: The door is operated from a ground handling panel with the aircraft on jacks or on its gear, and cannot be operated in flight.

assumptions.rationale: §5.7.6 states the door cannot be operated in flight, so the failure conditions manifest as pre-flight latents; the SDD does not state the exposure/check regime.

assumptions.text: SF-011-TL is correctly modelled as an AND of (loss of locking) and (loss of both confirmation paths), i.e. both must be lost for the stated top event.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the intent is loss of locking OR loss of confirmation, the top gate becomes OR and the single-point structure and DAL allocation change.

citations.quote: Eight independent locking pins are then driven through the latch bodies by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply

assumptions.rationale: The FC text names both 'locking and confirmation'; the SDD describes locking and sensing as separate provisions but does not state the FHA boolean relationship.

assumptions.text: The two dissimilar lock-sensing paths (proximity harness and mechanical visual indicator) are independent, so both must fail to lose confirmation.
assumptions.ifWrong: A common cause defeating both paths becomes an order-1 cut set for the confirmation branch, unacceptable for Catastrophic.

citations.quote: a proximity sensing harness reading pin position directly, and a mechanical linkage driving a visual indicator

assumptions.rationale: SDD claims dissimilar and independently routed sensing but independence is a claim to be tested, not established fact.

assumptions.text: SF-012-M requires both mechanical-lock-without-rated-tension AND failure of monitoring to reveal it for the erroneous (undetected) condition to stand.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the FC is intended as the mechanical fault alone regardless of monitoring, the monitoring branch drops and the top gate becomes single-branch OR.

citations.quote: A tension monitoring loop instruments every strap continuously. Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight

assumptions.rationale: The FCIM pairs this erroneous condition with an unaware case; the monitoring loop is the annunciation path but the FHA boolean is not stated in the SDD.

assumptions.text: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented run whose coverage is a recognised single-point limitation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the loop is later dual/segmented, the monitoring branch gains structure and is no longer an order-1 contributor.

citations.quote: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item

assumptions.rationale: SDD states the loop is single and its coverage is a recorded item; depth beyond the loop is not resolved by the architecture.

assumptions.text: Complete loss of longitudinal restraint requires loss of strap restraint at all stations OR a hold floor hard-point structural failure.
assumptions.ifWrong: The AND grouping and the number of independent strap-pair inputs change, altering whether an order-1 cut set exists in the strap branch.

citations.quote: Nine saddles with two straps each, with load paths sized such that the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours.

assumptions.rationale: §5.8.2/§5.8.3 describe nine saddles with two straps each and neighbour load-sharing, but do not state how many stations must fail for total loss; I modelled it as loss across the restraining set.

assumptions.text: The hold floor hard point is a single non-redundant load path and is therefore an order-1 (single-point) contributor to complete restraint loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If hard-point failure does not by itself constitute complete loss, this branch moves under the AND and the order-1 cut set disappears.

citations.quote: There is no redundancy in the hold floor hard points.

assumptions.rationale: §5.8.3 states no redundancy in the hard points; whether hard-point structural failure alone unrestrains the blade is a structural judgement I could not fully ground.

assumptions.text: The independent standby instrument shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primary display chain, so primary error plus standby failure is a valid AND (independent).
assumptions.ifWrong: If the standby shares a common element, the AND collapses toward an OR and erroneous primary information becomes a single-point path.

citations.quote: a standby instrument sharing nothing with the primaries

assumptions.rationale: §5.11.3 asserts independence; the tree's AND logic for the detectable-error branch depends on it holding.

assumptions.text: Erroneous flight/nav information can arise from an undetected common-source corruption that defeats the three-way reference-unit voting and dual-network comparison.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no credible common-mode source exists, that OR branch is removed and the top event reduces to the AND-protected path only.

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data.

assumptions.rationale: §5.11.2 describes three reference units and dual networks with voting, but the SDD does not enumerate common-mode error sources; I retained an OR branch for undetected common-mode error.

assumptions.text: Both alerting processing channels and both display presentation means must be lost for complete loss of crew alerting, i.e. the two channels are genuinely independent.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the two channels share a supply or route, that shared element becomes an order-1 cut set and the SF-019-TL tree needs a single-point basic event, breaking the no-SPOF requirement for a Catastrophic top.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019-TL AND gate 'Both alerting processing channels lost'

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states two independent alerting channels but does not enumerate their supply/routing separation, so the AND-gate independence is asserted not proven.

assumptions.text: The independent standby instrument uses a source, processing and supply that do not share the fault mode corrupting the primary displays.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the standby shares the fault (e.g. common DC essential loss coincident with a source fault), the AND gate collapses and erroneous-info-undetected becomes reachable through fewer independent failures.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-M2 AND gate 'Independent standby instrument does not reveal the discrepancy'

citations.quote: an independent standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.rationale: SDD claims the standby shares nothing with the primaries, but the DC essential bus also feeds one ADIRU and other critical loads, a potential common supply.

assumptions.text: ADIRU comparison/voting exists such that a single corrupted source is normally rejected, so an undetected erroneous source requires both a source fault and a voting failure.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no effective comparison exists, a single ADIRU source fault alone corrupts the primary path and the AND under 'Erroneous source data undetected' should reduce to an OR/single event.

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data

assumptions.rationale: Three reference units imply voting, but the SDD does not explicitly describe the comparison monitor, so the monitor-failure basic event is inferred.

assumptions.text: The two data network channels are the only delivery path to the displays and both must corrupt parameters for a network-induced erroneous presentation.
assumptions.ifWrong: A common network fault would make network corruption an order-1 contributor rather than the modelled AND, requiring restructure.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-M2 AND gate 'Data network delivers corrupted parameters'

citations.quote: The two network channels are routed on opposite sides of the fuselage and share no connector or penetration

assumptions.rationale: Dual redundant deterministic network is stated but per-channel corruption independence is not detailed beyond opposite-side routing.

assumptions.text: The two continuous fire-detection loops in each nacelle/APU zone are physically and functionally independent, so loss of both requires two independent basic events (AND gate).
assumptions.ifWrong: If the loop pair shares a common-cause (routing, connector, detection electronics), the per-zone AND collapses toward an order-1 cut set and the Catastrophic objective is not met by structure alone; a CMA/CCF group would be required.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-M and SF-020-M2 per-zone AND gates (nacelle loop A/B, APU loop A/B)

citations.quote: the two loops routed separately and an AND logic between them for warning

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the loops are routed separately with AND warning logic but does not quantify common-cause between them; the tree's Catastrophic no-single-point-of-failure structure depends on this.

assumptions.text: Fire detection and the crew-alerting/discharge circuits share the DC essential bus (detection) as a common power feed, modelled as a single common contributor to both top events.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection power is segregated per zone or backed up, the common DC-essential basic event overstates the shared contributor and should be split per zone.
assumptions.usedFor: 'Loss of DC essential supply' basic events in both SF-020-M and SF-020-M2

citations.quote: DC power from the essential bus to detection and from the hot battery bus to the discharge circuits

assumptions.rationale: The SDD assigns detection to the DC essential bus; loss of that supply defeats detection across all zones simultaneously.

assumptions.text: The hold smoke detection contributes to detection coverage but is left undeveloped, as the SDD treats it as nine stations without loop redundancy or internal decomposition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If hold smoke detection has redundancy or its own annunciation path, the undeveloped diamond should be expanded, changing coverage-loss contributors.
assumptions.usedFor: Hold smoke detection undeveloped events in both trees

citations.quote: The hold has smoke detection at nine stations along its length and no suppression

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes hold smoke detection only at station count and notes no suppression; no redundancy or internal architecture is given to develop the branch.

assumptions.text: Bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat detection are modelled as single (non-dual-loop) contributors, since the SDD specifies dual-loop only for nacelle and APU zones.
assumptions.ifWrong: If bleed-duct/gear-bay overheat detection is also dual-loop, those single basic events understate redundancy and should become AND gates.
assumptions.usedFor: Bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat basic events in both trees

citations.quote: Overheat detection is fitted to the bleed duct runs and to the main gear bays.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly assigns dual-loop AND logic to engine nacelles and APU; overheat detection on bleed ducts and gear bays is stated without loop redundancy.

assumptions.text: The common manifold and crossover valve form a single shared delivery path downstream of both cylinders and are modelled as an OR single-point-failure candidate.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the manifold/crossover carries internal redundancy, that OR branch collapses toward an AND and the single-point-failure concern for this Catastrophic top event is removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-TL 'Loss of shared oxygen delivery path' OR branch

citations.quote: Two high-pressure gaseous cylinders supply a common manifold with a crossover valve, feeding four quick-donning full-face masks

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes two cylinders on a common manifold with a crossover but does not resolve internal manifold redundancy, forcing a shared-path representation.

assumptions.text: Either cylinder alone can supply the crew for the required duration, so complete loss requires both cylinders unavailable (AND).
assumptions.ifWrong: If one cylinder cannot meet the required duration, a single cylinder loss becomes closer to a single-point contributor and the AND branch understates risk.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-TL 'Both oxygen cylinder sources unavailable' AND gate

citations.quote: either being capable of supplying the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states either cylinder is capable at reduced reserve; exact reserve adequacy is not quantified.

assumptions.text: Per-mask demand regulators are independent per station, so a single regulator fault is a partial loss and is excluded from this complete-loss top event.
assumptions.ifWrong: If regulators share a common failure path, a station-level regulator branch would need adding to the shared-path OR.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of per-mask regulator faults from SF-022-TL

citations.quote: Regulators are independent per mask.
